governing_table.code: International Building Code as adopted by the Oklahoma Uniform Building Code Commission (OAC 748:20-2), statewide minimum code for commercial construction; the same table is Table 403.1 of the Oklahoma-adopted International Plumbing Code (OAC 748:20-16)
governing_table.edition: 2024 (first printing), effective September 14, 2026, with Oklahoma amendments
governing_table.quote: 2902.1 Minimum number of fixtures. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 based on the actual use of the building or space. Uses not shown in Table 2902.1 shall be considered individually by the code official. The number of occupants shall be determined by this code. Exception: Plumbing fixtures shall not be required for buildings and facilities intended to be unoccupied and as approved by the code official, such as but not limited to, personal self-storage bays, shipping containers used only for on-site storage of materials, and structures housing equipment.
governing_table.adoption_quote: The Oklahoma Uniform Building Code Commission (the "OUBCC") hereby adopts the International Building Code®, 2024 Edition (IBC® 2024), first printing (August 2023) as amended and modified in this subchapter as the statewide minimum code for commercial building construction in the State of Oklahoma pursuant to 59 O.S. 1000.23.
governing_table.unamended_quote: All chapters and provisions within chapters, including exceptions, of the IBC® 2024 not specifically addressed within these rules as being modified, deleted, moved or removed are hereby adopted without modification as the statewide minimum code for commercial building construction within the State of Oklahoma
governing_table.note: Oklahoma's amendments to Chapter 29 (OAC 748:20-2-34) and to IPC Chapter 4 (OAC 748:20-16-9) were read on the Commission's own rule PDFs. They touch Section 2902.1/403.1 (an exception for unoccupied buildings), directional signs and drinking fountains only. They do not change Table 2902.1, Section 2902.1.1, Section 2902.2 or IPC Section 424.2, so those stand as published. The table rows and those sections were read on UpCodes' 'Oklahoma Building Code 2024' and 'Oklahoma Plumbing Code 2024' (secondary copies, which carry the Oklahoma amendments; codes.iccsafe.org serves no text to a plain fetch).

(59 O.S. § 1000.23(C)) | nor shall it prevent or take away from any state agencies or political subdivisions of the state the authority to amend such adopted codes to make changes necessary to accommodate local conditions; provided, such changes shall be approved by the Commission. (59 O.S. § 1000.29)

office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: See Section 424.2 (optional substitution, at most 50% of the men's required water closets in each toilet room)
office.quote: 2 | Business | Buildings for the transaction of business, nonmedical professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses | 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 | 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink

The ratio is applied to each sex's half of the occupant load under Section 2902.1.1. The 2024 edition moves ambulatory care and outpatient clinics to their own row with the same water-closet ratio.

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistical data show a different split. Where a shared room is designed for all genders, the count is worked out on the whole occupant load instead.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Exceptions: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex. Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number, for each sex.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the men's required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational uses and up to 50% in all other uses, including offices. Each urinal needs a partition on each side.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all other occupancies.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer, in a business occupancy of 25 or fewer, in a store of 100 or fewer, where single-user rooms are provided, or where a shared room is designed for all persons with a private compartment for each toilet and partitions at each urinal.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required to be designated by sex where single-user toilet rooms are provided in accordance with Section 2902.1.2. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code and for urinals in accordance with Section 405.3.5 of the International Plumbing Code.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 150 sq ft gross per occupant. Restaurant dining room (assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated, tables and chairs): 15 sq ft net. Classroom: 20 sq ft net. Oklahoma's amendments to Chapter 10 (OAC 748:20-2-15) do not touch Table 1004.5.
occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net [...] Business areas | 150 gross [...] Educational Classroom area | 20 net

privacy.text: Every toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door; every urinal needs side partitions that start no more than 12 inches above the floor and reach at least 60 inches.
privacy.quote: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. [...] Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not more than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.

100 occupants split in half = 50 of each sex. 50/25 = 2, rounded up to 2 for each sex. Urinals may replace at most 50% of the men's required toilets in a room: 50% of 2 = 1.00, so up to 1 (the code does not say how this share rounds; rounded down here).

200 occupants split in half = 100 of each sex. first 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50/50 = 1, total 3, rounded up to 3 for each sex. Urinals may replace at most 50% of the men's required toilets in a room: 50% of 3 = 1.50, so up to 1 (the code does not say how this share rounds; rounded down here).

400 occupants split in half = 200 of each sex. first 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 150/50 = 3, total 5, rounded up to 5 for each sex. Urinals may replace at most 50% of the men's required toilets in a room: 50% of 5 = 2.50, so up to 2 (the code does not say how this share rounds; rounded down here).

50 occupants split in half = 25 of each sex. 25/50 = 0.5, rounded up to 1 for each sex. Urinals may replace at most 67% of the men's required toilets in a room: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so up to 0 (the code does not say how this share rounds; rounded down here).

100 occupants split in half = 50 of each sex. 50/50 = 1, rounded up to 1 for each sex. Urinals may replace at most 67% of the men's required toilets in a room: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so up to 0 (the code does not say how this share rounds; rounded down here).

200 occupants split in half = 100 of each sex. 100/50 = 2, rounded up to 2 for each sex. Urinals may replace at most 67% of the men's required toilets in a room: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so up to 1 (the code does not say how this share rounds; rounded down here).

hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP) Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286 Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | Definition, Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish: The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings; [...]

This language simply means no modifications were made to this Chapter in the adoption of the 2024 IBC® and the Chapter stands, as published, as part of the statewide minimum code

access.state_standard: ICC A117.1-2017 with Supplement 1, referenced by Chapter 11 of the Oklahoma-adopted 2024 International Building Code (OAC 748:20-2-16; Chapter 35 lists 'ICC A117.1—17 with Supplement 1', and Oklahoma's Chapter 35 amendments in OAC 748:20-2-40 do not change it). Oklahoma has no separate state accessibility code; the federal 2010 ADA Standards apply alongside. UpCodes has no Oklahoma copy of A117.1-2017, so the standard was read on UpCodes' Ohio copy (Ohio's only amendment is to mirror height). Supplement 1 was not read.

differences.point: Vertical grab bar on the side wall
differences.state: A side-wall grab bar set must include an 18 inch vertical bar, bottom 39 to 41 inches above the floor, centre line 39 to 41 inches from the rear wall (A117.1-2017 604.5.1 and 604.5.1.2; required in wheelchair stalls by 604.9.6 and on both sides of ambulatory stalls by 604.10.4).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.5.1: only a horizontal side-wall bar. 'The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.'
differences.quote: Fixed side-wall grab bars shall include a horizontal bar complying with Section 604.5.1.1 and a vertical grab bar complying with Section 604.5.1.2. [...] A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.point: Toe clearance under the partitions of a wheelchair stall
differences.state: 12 inches high and 8 inches deep under the front partition and at least one side partition; not required at the front if the stall is deeper than 64 inches (wall-hung toilet) or 67 inches (floor-mounted), nor at the side if wider than 68 inches (A117.1-2017 604.9.5.1).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.4: 'a toe clearance of 9 inches (230 mm) minimum above the finish floor and 6 inches (150 mm) deep minimum beyond the compartment-side face of the partition'; exceptions at more than 62 / 65 inches deep and more than 66 inches wide.
differences.quote: The front partition and at least one side partition of wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members. Exceptions: Toe clearance at the front partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 64 inches (1625 mm) in depth with a wall-hung water closet, or greater than 67 inches (1700 mm) in depth with a floor-mounted water closet. Toe clearance at the side partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 68 inches (1725 mm) in width.

differences.state: At least 5 percent of the compartments in a toilet room must be wheelchair accessible; where toilets and urinals in the room total six or more, at least 5 percent of the compartments must also be ambulatory accessible (IBC 2024 Section 1110.2.4).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 213.3.1: 'Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition to the compartment required to comply with 604.8.1, at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.'
differences.quote: Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.
differences.note: The two rules differ only in rooms with more than 20 compartments.

differences.point: Where the wheelchair stall's door opening sits
differences.state: A117.1-2017 Table 604.9.3.1 gives two choices for a front door: the far edge of the opening 56 inches minimum from the side wall closest to the toilet, or 4 inches maximum from the side wall farthest from it. For a side door: 52 inches minimum from the rear wall (wall-hung) or 55 inches (floor-mounted), or 4 inches maximum from the front partition.
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 604.8.1.2: 'Where located in the front partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet. Where located in the side wall or partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the front partition.'
differences.quote: The farthest edge of the wheelchair accessible toilet compartment door opening shall be located in the front wall or partition or in the side wall or partition as required by Table 604.9.3.1. [...] Front Wall or Partition | From the side wall or partition closest to the water closet | 56 inches (1420 mm) minimum | or | From the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet | 4 inches (100 mm) maximum
differences.note: A door placed 4 inches from the far side wall meets both.

differences.point: Turning space in the restroom of a new building
differences.state: 67 inch turning circle in new buildings, 60 inches in existing buildings (A117.1-2017 304.3.1.1 and 304.3.1.2).
differences.federal: 2010 ADA Standards 304.3.1: 'The turning space shall be a space of 60 inches (1525 mm) diameter minimum.'
differences.quote: In new buildings and facilities, the turning space shall be a circular space with a 67-inch (1700 mm) minimum diameter. [...] In existing buildings and facilities, the turning space shall be a circular space with a 60-inch (1525 mm) minimum diameter.

differences.point: Family or assisted-use toilet room, and adult changing stations
differences.state: Assembly and mercantile buildings that need six or more toilets in total must add an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room (IBC 2024 Section 1110.2.1). Oklahoma amends Section 1110.4.1 to require an adult changing station there too, and in public or private parks and campgrounds.
differences.federal: The 2010 ADA Standards do not require a family room; 213.2.1 only describes one where provided ('Unisex toilet rooms shall contain not more than one lavatory, and two water closets without urinals or one water closet and one urinal.'). They have no adult changing station rule.
differences.quote: In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required. | 1110.4.1 Where required. Not fewer than one adult changing station shall be provided in the following locations: (A) Item 1. In assembly and mercantile occupancies, where family or assisted-use toilets or bathing rooms are required to comply with Section 1110.2.1. [...] (E) Item 5. Public or private parks and campgrounds.

access.same_as_federal: Stall sizes match: wheelchair stall 60 inches wide and 56 inches deep (wall-hung) or 59 inches (floor-mounted); ambulatory stall 35 to 37 inches wide and 60 inches deep; self-closing doors with pulls on both sides (A117.1-2017 604.9.2.1, 604.10.2, 604.9.3 against ADA 604.8.1.1, 604.8.2.1, 604.8.1.2).
access.process: No state registration or separate state plan review for accessibility was found. Accessibility is part of the building code, so the local building department checks it with the building permit. Where no local authority requires a building permit, the State Fire Marshal issues it ('In all geographical areas wherein no building permit is required by local authorities such permit shall be obtained from the State Fire Marshal's Office for all Use and Occupancy Classifications identified in the International Building Code', State Fire Marshal FAQ citing OAC 265:25-1-4(a)). For public buildings and buildings erected with public funds, 61 O.S. § 11 requires plans to 'provide facilities for people with disabilities. Such facilities shall conform with the codes and standards adopted by the State Fire Marshal'.

single_user.rule: Single-user toilet rooms count toward the required fixtures and must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex. Signs at required public toilet facilities must say whether the room is for males, females or all persons. Oklahoma adopts these sections without change.
single_user.quote: Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex. | 2902.4 Signage Required public toilet facilities shall be provided with signs that indicate whether the facility is to be used by males, by females, or by all persons regardless of sex. Signs shall be readily visible and located near the entrance to each toilet facility.

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed by the state building code. Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where a room with toilets and lavatories is designed for all persons and every toilet is in its own compartment with a door and every urinal has privacy partitions. The fixture count is then worked out on the whole occupant load, and each fixture type must meet the accessibility standard. Not available in public schools (see use_restrictions).
all_gender_shared.quote: Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code and for urinals in accordance with Section 405.3.5 of the International Plumbing Code. | Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1.

use_restrictions.rule: Two state laws. (1) 70 O.S. § 1-125: every public school and public charter school serving pre-kindergarten to 12th grade must designate each multiple occupancy restroom or changing area for the exclusive use of one sex (sex as on the original birth certificate) and give access to a single-occupancy restroom to anyone who does not wish to comply. (2) 57 O.S. § 509.7 (effective November 1, 2025): facilities operated by or contracted with the Department of Corrections must designate each multi-occupancy restroom for the exclusive use of females or males. No statute read applies to other government buildings or to private buildings: House Bill 3242 (2026), which would have covered public colleges, buildings owned or operated by a governmental subdivision and domestic violence shelters, passed the House on March 11, 2026 and was last placed on General Order in the Senate on April 22, 2026, with no enrolled version.
use_restrictions.quote: B. To ensure privacy and safety, each public school and public charter school that serves students in prekindergarten through twelfth grades in this state shall require every multiple occupancy restroom or changing area designated as follows: 1. For the exclusive use of the male sex; or 2. For the exclusive use of the female sex. C. Each public school or public charter school in this state shall provide a reasonable accommodation to any individual who does not wish to comply with the provisions of subsection B of this section. A reasonable accommodation shall be access to a single-occupancy restroom or changing room. | 57 O.S. § 509.7(B)(1): A covered entity shall designate each multi-occupancy restroom, changing room, and sleeping quarters for the exclusive use of either females or males.

other.rule: 63 O.S. § 1-1016A: restrooms in buildings built with public funds, reached from public corridors and built for public use, must be open to the public and labelled as public restrooms (not schools).
other.quote: Said public restrooms shall be clearly labeled by signs designating the same as public restrooms.

restrooms.confidence_note: Statutes read on the Legislature's complete-title PDFs (file dated November 11, 2026). Code sections read on UpCodes.

public_wage.law: None. The Oklahoma Minimum Wages on Public Works Act (40 O.S. §§ 196.1 to 196.14) was held unconstitutional in City of Oklahoma City v. State ex rel. Oklahoma Dept. of Labor, 918 P.2d 26 (Okla. 1995), and its sections were repealed by Laws 2015, c. 71, effective November 1, 2015. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded work.
public_wage.quote: §40-196.1. Unconstitutional – Repealed. NOTE: Entire Oklahoma Minimum Wages on Public Works Act (40 O.S. 1991, §§ 196.1 through 196.14) was held unconstitutional in the case of City of Oklahoma City v. State ex rel. Oklahoma Dept. of Labor, Okla., 918 P.2d 26 (1995). NOTE: This section repealed by Laws 2015, c. 71, § 1, eff. Nov. 1, 2015.
public_wage.note: Title 40 and Title 61 (public buildings and public works) were searched for 'prevailing wage': no section in force sets one. sam.gov was not opened; it is the federal site for Davis-Bacon wage determinations.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. Sales of tangible personal property are taxed at 4.5% state plus city and county tax at the delivery address. A remote seller with at least $100,000 of sales into Oklahoma in the preceding or current calendar year must collect it. If the seller does not, the buyer owes use tax at the same 4.5% plus local use tax.
shipped_goods.quote: Oklahoma sales tax is levied at 4.5% of the gross receipts from the sale or rental of tangible personal property and from the furnishing of specific services. If you ship goods, you will need to collect at the rate(s) in effect at the location where delivery occurs. | Under Oklahoma law, use tax must be paid on tangible personal property purchased and brought into this state for storage, use or consumption. If the property is brought into a county or municipality that also levies a use tax, the applicable county or municipal use tax must also be paid. | 68 O.S. § 1392(G)(1): A remote seller that had aggregate sales of products within this state or delivered to locations within this state subject to tax under Section 1354 or 1402 of this title worth at least One Hundred Thousand Dollars ($100,000.00) during the preceding or current calendar year shall collect and remit the tax imposed under Section 1354 or 1402 of this title.

freight.rule: Delivery charges are not taxed when stated separately on the invoice. They are taxed when included in the selling price.
freight.quote: (b) Separately-stated delivery charges. In every case where a delivery charge represents the cost of transporting the items sold from the vendor to the consumer, and is separately-stated on the invoice or statement, such charges are not subject to sales tax. (c) Delivery charges included in price. If delivery charges are included in the selling price of the tangible personal property sold, the charges are subject to sales tax. | 68 O.S. § 1352(18)(a)(5): [gross receipts are computed without deduction for] delivery charges and installation charges, unless separately stated on the invoice, billing or similar document given to the purchaser

install_labor.rule: Not taxed when the installation charge is shown separately in the seller's billing and books. A lump-sum price for property and installation is taxed in full. Construction, remodel or installation labor on a building is not among the 23 kinds of sale that 68 O.S. § 1354(A) taxes (item 21 taxes materials and taxable services sold to contractors).
install_labor.quote: (a) Where the quoted or advertised price is a lump sum for both property and installation or where billing and other records do not show separate charges for property and for installation, the measure of the tax is the total gross receipts received by the seller. (b) Where the seller has a standard retail sales price for his products and where the standard sales price is used both when making across-the-counter sales and when selling and installing the property, he may make a separate and additional charge for making the installation which, when shown separately in his billings and on his books, will not be subject to the sales tax.

furnish_and_install.rule: A contractor who improves real property and builds materials into it is the consumer of those materials and pays sales tax when buying them. Contractors on public contracts with a city, county, public school district or state college, and on certain private school and church contracts, may buy exempt. Whether installed toilet partitions count as an improvement to real property was not read in a Tax Commission source.
furnish_and_install.quote: (a) General rule. Contractors are defined by statute as consumer/users and must pay sales tax on all taxable services and tangible personal property, including materials, supplies, and equipment purchased to develop, repair, alter, remodel, and improve real property. | 68 O.S. § 1352(10): "Contractor" means any person who performs any improvement upon real property and who, as a necessary and incidental part of performing such improvement, incorporates tangible personal property belonging to or purchased by the person into the real property being improved

sales_tax.confidence_note: Rate, use tax and shipping rule read on the Tax Commission's own page; statutes on the Legislature's PDF. The Tax Commission rules (OAC 710:65-7-13, 710:65-19-70, 710:65-19-159, 710:65-1-7) were read on Cornell LII, a secondary copy. The Tax Commission's contractor exemption page notes a 2026 law (Senate Bill 44) letting certain exempt entities extend their exemption to contractors; its details were not read.

page.stalls_intro: Oklahoma's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a screen on each side.
page.stalls_after: These are the state minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. A city may set higher numbers. Where a shared room is built for all genders, the count is worked out on everyone in the building instead of on each half.
page.capacity: Oklahoma's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Oklahoma's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes, and Oklahoma's building rules add a national accessibility standard on top. The city checks access with the building permit. Where no city or county issues building permits, the State Fire Marshal does.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Oklahoma extras:** Oklahoma's rules ask for three things the federal ones do not. The side wall next to the toilet needs an 18 inch vertical grab bar as well as the horizontal one. The front partition and one side partition of the wheelchair stall need 12 inches of clear space above the floor, where the federal rule asks for 9. A new building's restroom needs a 67 inch turning circle, where the federal rule asks for 60. Stall widths and depths are the same in both.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and every urinal has privacy partitions. Oklahoma law requires shared restrooms in public schools, from pre-kindergarten to 12th grade, and in state correctional facilities to be designated for one sex.
page.public_jobs: Oklahoma has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded projects, under federal law.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Oklahoma, an installation charge is not taxed when it is shown separately from the partitions on the bill. A single price for partitions and installation is taxed in full. A contractor who supplies and installs partitions as part of the building pays the tax when buying them.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable at the rate for the delivery address. Freight is not taxed when it is listed separately on the invoice. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Oklahoma Tax Commission
